set.body:
Scheduling lane: research. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Research comparison retained; frozen exposure/eligibility rules apply. Not an engineering prerequisite or proof of behavioral recovery.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-18-best-recall-to-video-mapper.md §3 Phase 1a Step 5.

Arms: B0 timing-only floor; B1 BM25 and B2 embedding cosine, argmax over scenes; B1t/B2t the same on scene titles only; B3/B4 the current pipeline with and without fill (B3 is the primary development comparator). This ticket also owns the ledgered reproduction read of the historical B3 numbers.

Scope:
Run and score the retrieval arms under the repaired scorer; FilmFestival film identity as a cross-corpus development check.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Re-scoring the recorded B3 arm under the repaired scorer reproduces 63.8% pooled over 15 participants and 65.2% on development, or the commit explains every difference; this read is the pre-registered reproduction read.
2. Each arm emits one typed outcome for every manifest unit and is scored by the repaired scorer; each has a receipt (code hash, input hashes, config) committed as hashes.
3. FilmFestival film identity runs B1, B2 and B3/B4 on the coder index (T1) and the crowd index (T2), labelled cross-corpus development.
4. The Friends and Memento read-count ledgers still show zero reads.

Gate: every script in tools/recall-study/tests exits 0 (`for t in tools/recall-study/tests/test_*.py;
do python3 "$t" || exit 1; done`), new tests included; a named mutation witness per new guard; no
recall prose or participant text committed (hashes and aggregates only); fresh-context cold review;
the commit body states the evidence and what it does not establish.

Size: M.
set.title: [research] Phase 1a: retrieval baselines B0-B4 and B1t/B2t on Sherlock; film identity on FilmFestival
